o: It is C3, C4 and C5, mainly C4
Muscle migrated from cervical myotomes into the septum transversum, carrying its nerve.
It descends on scalenus anterior deep to the prevertebral fascia
The transverse cervical and suprascapular arteries cross it anterior to the fascia.
The right phrenic nerve passes through the oesophageal opening of the diaphragm
The right nerve passes through the vena caval opening in the central tendon. The left pierces the muscle of the left dome.
It is accompanied by the pericardiacophrenic artery because it has no regional artery in the mediastinum
True. The phrenic nerve takes its own artery, the pericardiacophrenic, because there is no regional artery along its mediastinal course. (Last's)

questions.s: Sensory fibres of the phrenic nerve supply the:
o: Costal pleura
Costal pleura is supplied by the intercostal nerves.
Fibrous pericardium and parietal serous pericardium
About a third of phrenic fibres are sensory.
Visceral serous pericardium
Last's: the visceral serous pericardium is insensitive.
Central parts of the diaphragmatic pleura and peritoneum
The periphery is supplied by the lower intercostal nerves.

questions.s: Regarding the vagi in the thorax:
o: The right vagus is in contact with the trachea
Last's: the vagi try to reach the midline. On the left the great arteries hold the nerve away.
The left vagus crosses the arch of the aorta deep to the left superior intercostal vein
The phrenic lies anterior, the vein crossing between.
Both vagi pass behind the lung roots
They contribute to the posterior pulmonary plexuses.
The anterior vagal trunk consists predominantly of right vagal fibres
The anterior trunk is mainly left vagal fibres and the posterior trunk mainly right, reflecting gut rotation.
The superficial part lies in front of the ligamentum arteriosum
The deep part lies to its right, in front of the left main bronchus.
The superficial part receives the cardiac branch of the left superior cervical sympathetic ganglion
And the inferior cervical cardiac branch of the left vagus.
Both recurrent laryngeal nerves contribute to the deep part
True. Both recurrent laryngeal nerves give cardiac branches to the deep cardiac plexus. (Last's)
Cardiac pain fibres travel with the vagus
Cardiac pain travels with sympathetic fibres (cell bodies in upper thoracic DRG). Vagal afferents mediate cardiovascular reflexes.
It lies on the necks of the ribs, anterior to the intercostal vessels and nerves
Lateral to the heads of the ribs.
The greater splanchnic nerve arises from the fifth to ninth ganglia
Lesser from T10 and T11, least from T12.
It enters the abdomen behind the lateral arcuate ligament
It passes behind the medial arcuate ligament on the front of psoas. The subcostal bundle passes behind the lateral arcuate ligament.
The least splanchnic nerve relays in a renal ganglion
Last's: an offshoot of the coeliac ganglion behind the renal artery.
White rami communicantes are found on all cervical nerves
White rami exist only from T1 to L2. Every spinal nerve receives a grey ramus.
Removal of the T1 ganglion risks Horner's syndrome
Last's: never remove T1 in upper limb sympathectomy.
Sympathetic fibres to the upper limb reach it mainly by running along the subclavian and axillary arteries
Last's: limb vessels get their sympathetic fibres from adjacent peripheral nerves, not from fibres running long distances along the arteries.
Removal of the L1 ganglion may compromise ejaculation
True. The L1 ganglion supplies the ductus deferens and seminal vesicles, so its removal may compromise ejaculation. (Last's)
The neurovascular bundle lies between the internal intercostal and innermost intercostal layers
The plane between the middle and inner layers.
From above down, the order in the costal groove is vein, artery, nerve
The nerve lies lowest and nearest the skin.
The first intercostal nerve gives a large lateral cutaneous branch
Last's: the first intercostal nerve has no lateral or anterior cutaneous branch.
Levatores costarum are supplied by posterior rami
Last's: the only thoracic wall muscles supplied by posterior rami.

questions.s: The posterior intercostal arteries of the first two spaces arise from the:
o: Superior intercostal artery
A branch of the costocervical trunk (second part of the subclavian).
Internal thoracic artery
It gives the anterior intercostal arteries of the upper six spaces.
Musculophrenic branch of the internal thoracic artery
The musculophrenic artery gives anterior intercostal branches to spaces 7 to 9.
Descending thoracic aorta
The aorta supplies the remaining nine spaces.
The radiate ligament has three bands, the central one forming the hypochordal bow
Last's: this explains the anterior arch of the atlas.
The first rib articulates with C7 and T1
Last's: the first rib articulates with T1 only, never with C7.
The 11th and 12th ribs have no costotransverse synovial joints
They have only ligamentous attachments.
Every costochondral joint is a primary cartilaginous joint
No movement occurs there.
The subclavian artery lies in the groove on the upper surface, in contact with the bone
Last's: the lower trunk of the brachial plexus lies in the groove. The artery usually lies a little higher, touching only the outer border.
Scalenus medius inserts into the scalene tubercle
Scalenus anterior inserts into the scalene tubercle. Scalenus medius inserts between the groove and the tubercle of the rib.
The first costal cartilage forms a synovial joint with the manubrium
It forms a primary cartilaginous joint, so the first ribs and manubrium move as one.
The subclavian vein lies in contact with the bone in front of the scalene tubercle
In its own groove, in front of scalenus anterior.

questions.s: Concerning the openings in the diaphragm:
o: The aortic opening lies at T12 behind the median arcuate ligament
It transmits the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct.
The oesophageal opening at T10 transmits the vagal trunks
And the oesophageal branches of the left gastric vessels.
The vena caval opening lies in the left leaf of the central tendon
It lies near the junction of the central and right leaves at T8.
The splanchnic nerves pierce the crura
True. The greater, lesser and least splanchnic nerves pierce the crura to reach the coeliac plexus. (Last's)
Septum transversum
It forms the central tendon.
Pleuroperitoneal membranes
Their failure is the commonest cause of congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
Third to fifth cervical myotomes
Muscle cells bring the phrenic nerve with them.
Dorsal mesentery of the oesophagus and body wall mesoderm
Last's lists all four sources.

questions.s: Regarding the nerve supply of the pleura and lungs:
o: The parietal pleura of the chest wall is supplied by the intercostal nerves
It is pain-sensitive.
The visceral pleura has only autonomic supply and is insensitive
True. Visceral pleura has only autonomic (vasomotor) supply and no pain fibres; parietal pleura is sensitive. (Last's)
Sympathetic fibres to the lungs cause bronchoconstriction
Sympathetic fibres (T2 to T6) are dilator to bronchi. Vagal parasympathetic fibres are constrictor.
The cough reflex from the bronchi is mediated by vagal afferents
Cell bodies in the inferior vagal ganglion.

questions.s: Concerning the veins of the superior mediastinum:
o: The arch of the azygos vein passes superficial to the right vagus and deep to the right phrenic nerve
Last's: the same relationship as the left superior intercostal vein on the left.
The left superior intercostal vein drains into the left brachiocephalic vein
It drains the second to fourth left spaces.
In the infant the left brachiocephalic vein may cross the trachea above the jugular notch
Relevant to tracheostomy in children.
The first intercostal space drains into the superior intercostal vein
The first space drains into the highest (supreme) intercostal vein, which joins the brachiocephalic vein.

questions.s: Regarding the innervation of the oesophagus:
o: The upper striated part is supplied from the nucleus ambiguus
Via the recurrent laryngeal nerves.
The lower smooth muscle part is supplied from the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus
Via the oesophageal plexus.
Its sympathetic supply in the upper part comes from the middle cervical ganglion with the inferior thyroid artery
True. The upper oesophagus receives sympathetic fibres from the middle cervical ganglion along the inferior thyroid artery. (Last's)
Pain from the oesophagus is carried only by the vagus
Last's: pain travels with both vagus and sympathetics.
The jugular notch lies at the level of T3
Last's: jugular notch T3, sternal angle T4 (the T4/5 disc), lower end of sternum T8.
The sternal angle lies at the level of T4
Last's gives T4 (at the T4/5 disc). It marks the lower limit of the superior mediastinum.
The lower end of the sternum lies at T8
True. The lower end of the sternum (xiphisternal joint) lies at about T8-9. (Last's)
The plane of the sternal angle marks the lower limit of the superior mediastinum
It passes to the T4/5 disc behind.

questions.t: Development of the heart and great vessels
o: It is derived from the left sixth arch artery
The right dorsal sixth arch disappears, so the right RLN hooks under the subclavian.
It closes after birth by contraction of its muscular wall
Stimulated by the rise in oxygen tension.
It becomes the ligamentum venosum
It becomes the ligamentum arteriosum. The ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum.
The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around it
Lying to its left.
